a:r.a:t: Metabolism Is the Sum of All Chemical Reactions in the Cell

p:cNvPr.descr: A simple diagram shows relationships between anabolic and catabolic metabolism, and their broader functions in biological systems. On the left is a large, upward blue arrow labeled “anabolism.” Below it is a blue box labeled “precursor molecules.” There is a list of molecules inside the box. It reads: “amino acids, sugars, fatty acids, nitrogenous bases.” The arrow points upward, and to the right are arrows showing the cycling of important molecules. A blue arrow diverges to the right from the main arrow to a gray circle containing text reading, “ADP + HPO4 superscript 2; NAD+; NADP+; FAD.” These are the products of anabolism. To the right of this circle is a red arrow, converging with a large red down arrow labeled “catabolism” on the right. These arrows curve down to an orange circle, directly below the gray one, which has text reading, “ATP, NADH, NADPH, and FADH2.” These are the outputs of catabolism. Below the orange circle is an orange box labeled “chemical energy.” Above the main blue arrow labeled anabolism is another blue box, which is labeled “cell macromolecules” and contains a list reading: “proteins, polysaccharides, lipids, nucleic acids.” On the right, there is a large red arrow labeled “catabolism.” Above, there is an orange box labeled “energy containing nutrients,” with a list reading, “carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.” The arrow points down to an orange box labeled “energy-depleted products,” with a list reading, “CO2, H2O, NH3.”
